objects.original: The function-form entropy A(g)=∫Φ(g²)dμ−Φ(∫g²dμ), genuine-gradient energy, compact smooth tests v, and the extended smooth test f.
objects.reconstructed: The same A(g) and D(g)=∫‖∇g‖²dμ with h(0)=0 and totalized real integrals.
objects.evidence: Lines 193–202 expand the same formula, including exactly the mass-subtraction term. The genuine gradient is the Riesz representative of the Fréchet derivative; the analytic function class ensures differentiability. The displayed Ent notation names this functional and does not imply that arbitrary μ is a probability.

domains.original: An arbitrary Borel measure on a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space. The all-compact premise uses totalized Bochner integrals; the target has genuine finite integrals. Chewi's probability setting is a specialization.
domains.reconstructed: A Borel measure on a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space, with the real integral set to zero on nonintegrable terms.
domains.evidence: Lines 48–49 and 191–202 impose the same carrier and no finiteness or probability axiom. Compact support alone does not imply integrability for arbitrary measures; lines 125–185 provide a.e. strong measurability and integrable dominators for these actual cutoff tests. For a probability law, compact smooth tests and their continuous compactly supported gradients are bounded and all relevant integrals are genuine.

quantifiers.original: Fix μ and C; assume the inequality universally for compact C∞ real tests, then conclude it for every C∞ real f with the three integrability conditions.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For arbitrary μ and C∈ℝ, the premise holds for every smooth compactly supported v, and the conclusion holds for every admissible smooth f.
quantifiers.evidence: Lines 191–202 place the universal compact-test premise before f and use the same μ and C throughout. Lines 206–214 apply the single premise for every n, only to the valid f_n.

assumptions.original: The compact smooth premise has coefficient 2C. The target is smooth with f and its genuine gradient in L² and Φ(f²) in L¹, without restrictions on the sign of f or C, or positive mass.
assumptions.reconstructed: A(v)≤2C D(v) for all smooth compact v, and f is smooth with the same L²/L²/L¹ requirements.
assumptions.evidence: The premise is genuinely C∞, not the stronger demand that it hold for all compact C² tests. The target also stays C∞; lines 204–205 only lower regularity internally for the integral-limits prerequisite. Continuity of Φ at zero and the real-order limit step do not require a sign or nonzero-mass assumption.

conclusion.original: The same function-form LSI with genuine integrable terms and unchanged coefficient holds on the indicated noncompact smooth analytic domain.
conclusion.reconstructed: A(f)≤2C D(f) for every admissible f.
conclusion.evidence: Lines 203–217 apply the inequality on compact smooth f_n and pass the mass, entropy-integrand and energy terms to their limits. Integrability at f is exactly the L²/L²/L¹ input; Real.continuous_mul_log handles the mass normalization without division, including at zero.

scopes.original: An original sufficient implementation of the source's density step, classically interpreted for the probability-law specialization, with a separate totalized arbitrary-measure generalization. No maximal closed form domain or completion of Exercise 1.7 is claimed.
scopes.reconstructed: A conditional extension from compact smooth tests to the specified smooth analytic class under the stated integral convention, not an unconditional LSI or a Poincaré inequality.
scopes.evidence: The packet binds the declaration as the proof edge for extend-compact-smooth-lsi. The source does not specify the explicit analytic class or the totalized generalization. Finite dimension is used for support compactness at lines 210–214, not by the shared integral-limits theorem.

constant_dependencies.original: The fixed real C of the compact hypothesis is retained verbatim, with factor 2; any cutoff derivative bound is internal to the prerequisite.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The identical coefficient 2C in both the compact-test premise and the extended inequality.
constant_dependencies.evidence: Lines 194–202, 206–209 and 215–217 transport the identical coefficient via he.const_mul (2 * C). There is no dependence of the output coefficient on f, n, mass, dimension, or the separately obtained cutoff derivative constant.

review_evidence: Independently checked Sinho Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling, August 20, 2026, PDF SHA-256 8818e8fb40c07bd70651bafe10e8ec4500197c836928330b90025ca47da52fae (matched the PDF bytes at https://chewisinho.github.io/main.pdf). Section 2.1.1, printed pp. 48–49 / PDF pp. 60–61, states the 2C function-form LSI on compact smooth real tests in the Euclidean Langevin probability setting and refers to density for wider classes without fixing one. Example 1.2.27 confirms the entropy subtraction used in that specialization. The packet's exact sufficient domain and its totalized arbitrary-measure premise are original ASTIS, not an exact statement from Chewi or a generalization with classical integrals on every compact test. Read the whole bound LogSobolevCutoff.lean module (workspace byte digest 25d865b9f731b83fa0af7fd32c183c2630c9fa86f5e36c4d8c1b4cddcd088cbc) and checked the cutoff API. Both authored formula steps match: f_n is compact and smooth in finite dimension, its own three integrands are genuinely integrable by the prerequisite's envelopes, and the three scalar limits plus continuity of Φ at zero and closedness of order give the same coefficient (lines 203–217). Exercise 1.7, printed p. 43 / PDF p. 55, still requires the perturbative KL/Fisher-information or entropy/energy linearization and the Poincaré conclusion; the extension only allows noncompact smooth tests, such as the square root of a small positive perturbation of 1 on a probability space.
